title: Rizia/Turn 2/Pre-Meeting Talk With Vina Or Estela

4.speaker: Estela Toras
4.text: "I'm surprised you haven't died of boredom yet."

6.speaker: Player_Romus
6.text: "I'm discussing the fate of the country. How could I be bored?"

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: She lit two cigarettes and handed one to me.

10.speaker: Estela Toras
10.text: "The fate of the country depends on tax rates and trade agreements, I see. Wake me when there's a war."

11.speaker: Estela Toras
11.text: "If your uncle was any more pleased with the sound of his own voice, he'd be a parakeet."

12.speaker: Estela Toras
12.text: "Seriously, I hope you're faring well thus far."

14.speaker: Player_Romus
14.text: "Did you know about the Golden Guard?"

16.speaker: Estela Toras
16.text: "You're asking the wrong person. Don't forget, he positively loathes me."

17.speaker: Estela Toras
17.text: "Of course, darling. They're a little unnerving at first, but that Titus fellow would take a bullet for you."

18.speaker: Narrator
18.text: She stormed off, leaving me to my own thoughts. Before I knew it, it was time for the council meeting.

19.speaker: Player_Romus
19.text: "Good to see you outside of the council chambers. Do you have any questions about the past few meetings?"

20.speaker: Estela Toras
20.text: "With that said, he was nothing but loyal to your father. And that loyalty extends to anyone with the last name Toras, personal squabbles aside."

21.speaker: Estela Toras
21.text: "Even more so for Vina, I imagine."

22.speaker: Estela Toras
22.text: "Now picture your daughter having to fill her head with that drivel. Aren't you glad you kept her off the Council?"

28.speaker: Player_Romus
28.text: "I can tell she's struggling, but she'll learn."

29.speaker: Player_Romus
29.text: "I don't know. Maybe it would have been a valuable experience."

30.speaker: Player_Romus
30.text: "I bet you're wishing you'd never asked to come to my meetings, right?"

31.speaker: Vina Toras
31.text: "What are you talking about? It's been fascinating!"

32.speaker: Narrator
32.text: To my left, I saw Vina reading a book on a bench beneath a decorative stone arch. In the date palm grove to my right, I caught a glimpse of my mother.

33.speaker: Player_Romus
33.text: "Yes, she's lucky not to have to deal with it all."

34.speaker: Player_Romus
34.text: "Sorry if Uncle Hugo made you feel uncomfortable the other day."

35.speaker: Player_Romus
35.text: "Yes, I'm starting to regret giving in to her."

37.speaker: Estela Toras
37.text: "Let's hope it never comes to that. It'd be a waste of a spectacular torso."

38.speaker: Player_Romus
38.text: "We're sitting on so much money. Why didn't Father do anything with it?"

41.speaker: Estela Toras
41.text: "He was paralyzed at the end. By the weight of all the decisions he had made, and the fear of making a faulty one."

42.speaker: Estela Toras
42.text: "Nearly losing you had a momentous effect on him. On us both."

43.speaker: Narrator
43.text: A bell chimed in the distance. It was time for the meeting to begin.

44.speaker: Player_Romus
44.text: "I *did* lose my wife. I managed to keep myself together."

45.speaker: Player_Romus
45.text: "I can respect that. I haven't been the same since losing Lena."

46.speaker: Player_Romus
46.text: "And now I've got to pick up all of his slack."

48.speaker: Player_Romus
48.text: "Listen, I'll give the book back to you. But don't let anyone else catch you reading it."

49.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
49.text: Take the book and look at it.

51.speaker: Vina Toras
51.text: "That's okay. I know he means well."

55.speaker: Narrator
55.text: She hurriedly shoved the book she was reading into her handbag. On the cover were the words "Ce Faximi" -- "What Are We To Do?" in Rizian.

58.speaker: Narrator
58.text: Vina sheepishly fished the book out of her bag and handed it to me.

59.speaker: Narrator
59.text: I took a closer look at the cover. Beneath the title were the words, "A Collection of Proposals by L. Chavatangakwunua."

60.speaker: Player_Romus
60.text: "The uprising didn't succeed because the Rizian people knew what was good for them. A strong leader and strong laws."

63.speaker: Player_Romus
63.text: "This had better not be what I think it is."

65.speaker: Player_Romus
65.text: "It failed because it lacked cohesion. Every faction was fighting for something different."

66.speaker: Vina Toras
66.text: "Look at what he writes here. True systemic change can only be accomplished with the wholehearted support of the working class."

67.speaker: Player_Romus
67.text: "Workers did join the protests. But yes, the initial spark came from naval officers."

68.speaker: Player_Romus
68.text: "You don't need to bother with this. You're a princess, not an intellectual."

69.speaker: Player_Romus
69.text: "Enroll in etiquette classes. Learn how to bake. The possibilities are endless."

70.speaker: Vina Toras
70.text: "You can't control what I read, you know. I'm a grown woman."

71.speaker: Player_Romus
71.text: "All right. But don't let anyone else catch you reading it."

72.speaker: Player_Romus
72.text: "It would be easier if I knew whom I could trust."

74.speaker: Vina Toras
74.text: "It's not as extreme as his later work. He wrote it right before changing his last name to Malenyev."

75.speaker: Vina Toras
75.text: "He changed it to Malenyev right after this was published."

76.speaker: Player_Romus
76.text: "This is dangerous propaganda, Vina. Don't you realize Malenyev and his followers hate people like you and me?"

77.speaker: Vina Toras
77.text: "Isn't that why it's important to know how they think?"

78.speaker: Player_Romus
78.text: "You know, I've always been curious about Malenyevism. Do you think it's compatible with monarchy?"

79.speaker: Vina Toras
79.text: "Do you think that's why the uprising in Rizia failed? Because workers weren't the ones leading the charge?"

80.speaker: Vina Toras
80.text: "You wouldn't allow me onto the council. There are only so many balls I can attend. What else am I supposed to do?"

81.speaker: Vina Toras
81.text: "Endlessly dull, you mean. Will you please give me my book back?"

82.speaker: Narrator
82.text: Vina gave me a conspiratorial nod.

85.speaker: Vina Toras
85.text: "This was one of his first tracts. He wrote it right before changing his name to Malenyev."

87.speaker: Vina Toras
87.text: "They thought that was what they wanted. Because nobody bothered to teach them otherwise."

88.speaker: Vina Toras
88.text: "And aristocrats working for their own gain, right? Like your kidnappers."

89.speaker: Player_Romus
89.text: "This is no way for a Toras to be carrying on. I'm taking this book away from you."

90.speaker: Player_Romus
90.text: "I knew you'd learn more off the council than on it. Keep it up."

91.speaker: Estela Toras
91.text: "Chin up, now. I'll see you at supper."

92.speaker: Narrator
92.text: My mother raised her parasol and strode away.

94.speaker: Narrator
94.text: Vina stared at me in disbelief for a moment.

97.speaker: Narrator
97.text: She took the book and walked away, leaving me to my own thoughts. Before I knew it, it was time for the council meeting.

100.speaker: Vina Toras
100.text: "It was just lying around in the library. One of his supporters must have had it translated into Rizian."

101.speaker: Vina Toras
101.text: "Of course, he wrote this right before he changed his name to Malenyev."

103.speaker: Vina Toras
103.text: "I've read all her writings already. And this one applies to our modern era far more."

105.speaker: Narrator
105.text: Vina stared at me in disbelief for a second, then smiled.

106.speaker: Player_Romus
106.text: "No. Find another use of your time."

107.speaker: Player_Romus
107.text: "It's overwhelming at times. But I trust the council to help me decide."

108.speaker: Narrator
108.text: She lowered the black lace parasol she was holding and linked her arm through mine.

109.speaker: Narrator
109.text: She reached into her handbag and pulled out a slim paperback. On its cover were the words "Ce Faximi", or "What Are We To Do?" in Rizian.

113.speaker: Vina Toras
113.text: "I have plenty. But I'll figure them out on my own time."

114.speaker: Vina Toras
114.text: "All of this council stuff is old hat for you, isn't it? You've even served with some of the same people before."

116.speaker: Narrator
116.text: I took a closer look at the cover. Beneath the title were the words, "A Collection of Proposals by L. Chavatangakwunua."

120.speaker: Estela Toras
120.text: "I found this in Vina's room after she went to lunch. Her way of rebelling against you for not letting her on the council, I assume."

121.speaker: Player_Romus
121.text: "Is this what I think it is?."

122.speaker: Estela Toras
122.text: "She was too quiet. I worried she was up to something."

123.speaker: Player_Romus
123.text: "I'm the king. Every decision I make is the right decision."

125.speaker: Player_Romus
125.text: "What were you doing snooping around my daughter's room?"

127.speaker: Estela Toras
127.text: "I remember hearing that name a long time ago. Before he changed it to Malenyev."

129.speaker: Vina Toras
129.text: "This must be overwhelming for you as well. So many decisions to make."

130.speaker: Player_Romus
130.text: "A long time ago. Frankly, they should have retired by now."

131.speaker: Vina Toras
131.text: "Any good monarch listens to the will of the public. Queen Lyza always said that."

132.speaker: Player_Romus
132.text: "Queen Lyza wasn't a saint. She had her flaws."

134.speaker: Vina Toras
134.text: "By the time she was my age, she'd already been queen for a year. Imagine!"

135.speaker: Player_Romus
135.text: "Yes, it's easy enough. I'm the king. What I say goes."

136.speaker: Player_Romus
136.text: "Don't you worry about me. Focus on keeping your own head above water."

137.speaker: Vina Toras
137.text: "I know. But it's still an inspiring legacy to live up to."

138.speaker: Player_Romus
138.text: "It's different now that I'm the one in charge."

139.speaker: Player_Romus
139.text: "Of course I will. They're the best hope we have for giving Rizians an actual voice."

141.speaker: Player_Romus
141.text: "I was naive back then. Now I don't know whom I can trust."

144.speaker: Vina Toras
144.text: "Ms. Werner and Mr. Esquibel may be old, but what they were saying made a lot of sense to me."

145.speaker: Player_Romus
145.text: "A good monarch listens. A great monarch acts."

146.speaker: Player_Romus
146.text: "And if the will of the public is for there to be no monarch at all? What then?"

147.speaker: Vina Toras
147.text: "If you rule as well as she did, that won't ever become a problem."

150.speaker: Player_Romus
150.text: "I'm not against the opposition because of House Sazon. I'm against it because it's the opposition."

151.speaker: Player_Romus
151.text: "I'll take their opinions into consideration. But I'm the one with the final say."

152.speaker: Player_Romus
152.text: "I might, but I don't want anything to do with your friend Mr. Sazon."

153.speaker: Vina Toras
153.text: "Why do you have it out for House Sazon? Just because one duke plotted against the king doesn't mean the whole family is evil."

154.speaker: Player_Romus
154.text: "Lucas put a taint on his entire house. I won't discuss this further."

155.speaker: Player_Romus
155.text: "It's not all of the Sazons. Manus in particular strikes me as suspicious."

156.speaker: Vina Toras
156.text: "Suspicious? He wants to work with you. Why not at least hear what he has to say?"

159.speaker: Vina Toras
159.text: "What do you think of the House of Delegates? Will you go talk to them?"

160.speaker: Player_Romus
160.text: "The only reason I would do that is to find out the opposition's weaknesses."

162.speaker: Player_Romus
162.text: "The Sazons have never truly been a royal house. Their ancestor had no claim to the throne."

163.speaker: Narrator
163.text: A clock chimed in the distance. It was time for the meeting.

164.speaker: Vina Toras
164.text: "I can't imagine how it feels to hold all that power."

166.speaker: Vina Toras
166.text: "The royal heir doesn't always have to be the king's son. Sometimes there are special circumstances."

167.speaker: Vina Toras
167.text: "Um... not really. A society ruled by a king is the embodiment of everything Malenyevists hate."

168.speaker: Vina Toras
168.text: "But it's useful to know how they think, isn't it?"

169.speaker: Vina Toras
169.text: "I mean... of course it's all rubbish. But it does make one think."

170.speaker: Vina Toras
170.text: "The student and workers' movement was more aligned with Malenyevism, but the nobles who rebelled were in favor of Arcasian democracy."

174.speaker: Estela Toras
174.text: "That's an underreaction, wouldn't you say? Malenyevist tracts belong in an incinerator, not your daughter's bedroom."

175.speaker: Estela Toras
175.text: "I can see why he changed it to 'Malenyev', That's one unholy mass of letters."

176.speaker: Player_Romus
176.text: "There were Malenyevists involved in the '26 uprising, weren't there? It could be useful to learn how the enemy thinks."

177.speaker: Player_Romus
177.text: "You're right, Mother. I'm sure it's pure garbage."

178.speaker: Player_Romus
178.text: "Vina's a smart girl. She wouldn't be reading this if there weren't value in it."

180.speaker: Player_Romus
180.text: "I see. Well, better this than Arcasian garbage."

182.speaker: Player_Romus
182.text: "The man had some good ideas. Maybe his vision of a more egalitarian society isn't entirely incompatible with monarchy."

183.speaker: Estela Toras
183.text: "My dear, I'm no scholar, but I do know there's a direct correlation between this fellow's line of thinking and royal beheadings."

184.speaker: Estela Toras
184.text: "The workers and students were inspired by Malenyevism. The nobles who got involved were pushing for Arcasian-style democracy."

185.speaker: Estela Toras
185.text: "I'm no scholar myself. But I do know the former leads to more royal beheadings than the latter."

186.speaker: Estela Toras
186.text: "It's more than that, dear. Garbage won't cut off your head in the middle of the night."

187.speaker: Estela Toras
187.text: "So what should I do with the book?"

188.speaker: Estela Toras
188.text: "My dear, I'm no scholar, but I do know there's a direct correlation between this fellow's line of thinking and royal beheadings."

189.speaker: Estela Toras
189.text: "They're like cannons at that age. You've got to mind the direction they're pointed in, or there'll be hell to pay when they go off."

190.speaker: Estela Toras
190.text: "Very well. But I do suggest having a chat with her about this."

191.speaker: Narrator
191.text: She put the book back in her purse.

193.speaker: Player_Romus
193.text: "Put it back where you found it. Vina's allowed to read what she wants in her free time."

194.speaker: Player_Romus
194.text: "This is dangerous propaganda. You were right to bring it to my attention."

195.speaker: Estela Toras
195.text: "I try to stay out of ideological debates. But I do know there's a direct correlation between this line of thinking and royal beheadings."

196.speaker: Player_Romus
196.text: "Give it to me. Vina shouldn't be exposed to such ideas."

199.speaker: Narrator
199.text: She handed the book to me.
